messages:
mira: heads up — after rolling nvidia-container-toolkit from 1.12.1 -> 1.13.0 to gpu-nodepool-us-west2, a bunch of GPU pods fail to start. noticed in the last 30m, ~12 nodes impacted across two ASGs. rollback to 1.12.1 makes pods start again.

mira: error snippet from kubelet/containerd logs:
```
May 29 11:02:14 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1234]: ContainerStart failed for pod gpu-train-7: failed to setup network and devices: failed to mount "/run/nvidia/host-files-for-container.d/libcuda.so.1": stat /run/nvidia/host-files-for-container.d/libcuda.so.1: no such file or directory
May 29 11:02:14 ip-10-0-3-45 containerd[5678]: time="2026-05-29T11:02:14Z" level=error msg="failed to create shim: mount error: path /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.1: permission denied"
```

mira: also seeing permission denied on /dev/nvidia0 in a couple of nodes, plus one multi-GPU job got NCCL "unhandled cuda error" after retry. :grimacing:

ash: which AMI/kernel/driver combo are these nodes on? did we also bump the host driver or only toolkit?

mira: only toolkit changed in the daemonset (image: nvidia/toolkit:1.13.0). Host driver still 525.85.05 on the fleet (ubuntu-22.04 kernels: 5.15.x).

ben: we ran into a similar happening last quarter but that was when toolkit tried to create symlinks under /run/nvidia concurrently with multiple container starts. could be a race where the host-files-for-container dir isn't populated before containerd tries to mount.

sre_lead: can you paste the full containerd create/start stacktrace and the toolkit logs from the nvidia ds on the affected nodes? also which runtime (runc/crun) are these using?

mira: attaching the condensed ds logs (snippet):
```
2026-05-29T11:01:58Z toolkit-daemon info: creating host files for container 5f3c... (/run/nvidia/host-files-for-container.d/5f3c...)
2026-05-29T11:01:58Z toolkit-daemon warn: failed to link /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /run/nvidia/host-files-for-container.d/5f3c.../libcuda.so.1: EEXIST
2026-05-29T11:01:58Z toolkit-daemon error: open /run/nvidia/host-files-for-container.d/5f3c.../libcuda.so.1: permission denied
```

mira: runtime is runc 1.1.4 for these nodes. containerd 1.7.x.

devops: is AppArmor or a stricter seccomp profile enabled on these nodes? permission denied suggests kernel LSM is blocking link/creation.

mira: AppArmor is in enforced mode, but unchanged. this started exactly after toolkit roll. tried disabling AppArmor on one node (for a quick test) — that node succeeded in starting GPU containers.

gpu-ops: sounds like toolkit 1.13 changed how it performs bind mounts / symlink creation. could be both a timing and permission model change. we should add a canary to staging with same kernel+driver and run a tight churn test.

ash: agree. immediate mitigation: pin toolkit to 1.12 on prod pools, rollback DS, drain and reprovision any nodes updated to 1.13.

mira: rolling rollback now to 1.12.1 (started). will mark affected ASGs to avoid automatic rolling by cluster-autoscaler.

ops-bot: [automated] rollback deployment "nvidia-toolkit-daemonset" initiated by mira at 2026-05-29T11:11:03Z :repeat:

ben: FYI we saw NCCL hangs when libnvidia-ml didn't bind correctly — multi-GPU epochs stalled, so this is high priority for batch infra.

sre_lead: action items:
- rollback prod -> 1.12.1 (mira) [in progress]
- run churn canary in staging with 1.13 + disabled apparmor to confirm LSM interaction (ash)
- file bug w/ NVIDIA and include ds logs + kernel/driver matrix (gpu-ops)
- add pre-mount healthcheck hook in our toolkit DS that waits for host-files dir to be populated before creating containers (devops)

devops: adding a pre-start init container suggestion:
```
- name: nvidia-host-files-wait
  image: busybox
  command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "for i in $(seq 1 10); do [ -d /run/nvidia/host-files-for-container.d ] && exit 0 || sleep 1; done; exit 1"]
```

mira: will run the rollback, then post a short incident update. if rollback completes cleanly we'll keep nodes pinned until vendor fix.

gpu-ops: also check kernel upgrade schedule — new toolkit may assume newer kernel capabilities (ioctl perms). don't auto-upgrade kernels in nodepools until we validate.

ash: marking this for the weekly infra retro and adding to the runbook. assigning to gpu-ops for vendor escalation. tagging: @gpu-ops @sre_lead

mira: rollback complete, 9/9 affected pods restarted successfully after DS rollback and node restart. leaving ASGs pinned for now. will update after vendor response.

sre_lead: thanks — file the post-incident note and include reproduction steps. closing the thread here unless we get vendor patches. :thumbsup:
